title: Persist an ExecutionAttempt record with a per-task generation counter
description:
Objective: give every execution of a task a durable identity, so a later call can be told whether it belongs to the current attempt or a superseded one. This is the foundation the rest of the epic fences on.

Deliverable: an ExecutionAttempt type in packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts and a new packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts holding it, persisted under .moe/attempts/. Fields: id, taskId, workerId, runnerId, generation (monotonic per task, starting at 1), workspace, phase (running, finalizing, reconciling, closed), startedAt, lastPhaseAt, and optional process start time and host for later reattachment. Copy the durable-first ordering already proven in state/resourceStore.ts: write the record before the state transition it enables, and make a second pass repair a partial write rather than duplicating it.

Not in scope: wiring into claim, complete or release; any tool registration; any client change. Those are separate sibling tasks. This task adds the record and its store only.

Verification: npx vitest run src/state/attemptStore.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: ExecutionAttempt is declared in packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts with the phase union running, finalizing, reconciling, closed
packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts creates, reads, updates the phase of and lists attempts, persisting one JSON file per attempt under .moe/attempts/
openAttempt allocates a generation that is strictly greater than every prior attempt for that task, proven by a test opening three attempts in sequence
A new attempt written while a prior attempt for the same task is still running is rejected with a named error rather than silently overwriting it
Re-running the write path over a half-written record repairs it instead of creating a duplicate, proven by a durability test in the style of resourceStore.durability.test.ts
npx vitest run src/state/attemptStore.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: Store layer only: no tool registration in tools/index.ts and no change to claim, complete or release handlers.
Follow the persist-before-transition ordering in state/resourceStore.ts; do not invent a second persistence idiom.

implementationPlan.description: STUDY THE IDIOM YOU ARE REQUIRED TO COPY. Read-only, no edits. A task rail forbids inventing a second persistence idiom, so read the existing one before writing anything. (a) Read packages/moe-daemon/src/state/resourceStore.ts, especially its header comment, which states the contract in one line: stateless functions taking the state handle first, every mutation under the state mutex, and a write path of writeEntity then map.set then appendActivity then emit. Persist before the transition the record enables - that ordering is the whole point and it is what makes a crash recoverable. (b) Read packages/moe-daemon/src/state/persistence.ts lines 323-348: writeEntity validates the id against path traversal, creates the kind directory itself with recursive mkdir, and finishes with an atomic write through a temp file and rename. Two consequences for this task: the new attempts directory needs no scaffolding anywhere, and a torn half-written JSON file is not the failure mode to design for - the real one is a record that reached disk before the process died without the in-memory map or any follow-up ever happening. (c) Read loadEntities at persistence.ts:38 and how StateManager.load uses it for resources at line 1038, plus the resources map declaration at line 367. (d) Read src/state/resourceStore.durability.test.ts lines 1-60 for the failure-injection style this task must reuse: a ToolTestHarness, a spy that makes the first writeEntity for one kind throw, and assertions that both the in-memory accessor AND the on-disk file are untouched. (e) Read src/tools/toolTestHarness.ts for init, setupMoeFolder, createEpic, createTask and cleanup. Write the findings into the step note. No source edits in this step.
implementationPlan.note:
READ-ONLY STUDY. No source edits. Findings, all measured in this checkout today:

(a) resourceStore.ts (430 lines) — header states the contract verbatim: "stateless functions taking the state handle first; every mutation runs under state.mutex (tool dispatch provides it...)" and "Write path per mutation: writeEntity -> map.set -> appendActivity -> emit." persistResource (line 102) is the single funnel: stamps updatedAt, `await state.writeEntity('resources', id, resource)`, THEN `state.resources.set(...)`, THEN emit. Mutations operate on a private deep copy (copyResource, line 87) precisely so a thrown write cannot have altered published state — this is the mechanism the two injected-failure tests assert, not just the ordering.

(b) persistence.ts writeEntity at line 323 (not 323-348 exactly, body runs 323-348): `validateEntityId(id)` first (util/sanitize.ts:101 — rejects anything outside /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/ and >128 chars, so a path separator throws INVALID_INPUT before any fs call), then `fs.mkdirSync(dir, {recursive:true})` for the kind dir, then a resolve+startsWith prefix re-check, then fileWatcher.ignorePath, then `atomicWriteJsonAsync` (temp file + rename, async so the rename-retry backoff does not block the event loop). Consequences confirmed: .moe/attempts/ needs zero scaffolding, and a torn half-JSON is not reachable — the real failure mode is a record that landed on disk with nothing following it, so repair = idempotent re-open keyed on a caller-suppliable id.

(c) loadEntities at persistence.ts:38 — `if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return map;` then per-file try/catch that logs+skips a bad file (one corrupt record never bricks load). Keys the map by the record's own `id` field. resources map declared StateManager.ts:367; loaded StateManager.ts:1038 `this.resources = loadEntities<ResourceState>(path.join(this.moePath, 'resources'))`. StateManager.writeEntity is a public instance method at line 900 delegating to the persistence function — that is what makes `vi.spyOn(h.state, 'writeEntity')` able to intercept a store's writes.

(d) resourceStore.durability.test.ts:1-60 — style is: ToolTestHarness + setupMoeFolder({schemaVersion:6}) + createEpic/createTask + `await h.state.load()`; postToGeneral/postToRoleChannel/postSystemMessage stubbed; failNextResourceWrite() binds the real method, then spies writeEntity to throw once for a matching `kind` and delegate afterwards; each test asserts BOTH the in-memory accessor AND the on-disk bytes (readResource()) are untouched, and one also asserts the activity event was never appended.

(e) toolTestHarness.ts (139 lines) — init() makes an os.tmpdir mkdtemp project + `new StateManager({projectPath})`; setupMoeFolder creates .moe + epics/tasks/workers/proposals dirs and project.json (settings.approvalMode CONTROL), plus a real `file.ts` for the submit_plan existence gate; createEpic -> 'epic-1'; createTask -> 'task-1' with BACKLOG/MEDIUM defaults, overridable; createWorker -> 'worker-1'; cleanup() rmSync -r -f.

Extra facts that shape steps 2-4:
- Named-error precedent is 4-arg MoeError with an explicit codeName and a REUSED numeric code: taskStore.ts:140 (MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT + 'PLAN_REVISION_EXHAUSTED') and :475 ('PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH'). No enum member was added for either. MAX_PLAN_REVISION = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (taskStore.ts:47) is the safe-integer-domain precedent.
- Task.planRevision (schema.ts:613) is the additive-field precedent: optional, documented, explicitly "no migration, no schemaVersion bump", domain called out as shared with the Kotlin/JSON clients' Long. CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 6 (schema.ts:236).
- generateId (util/ids.ts) = `${prefix}-${uuid-without-dashes}` (full 128-bit UUID) — the repo id shape for a generated attempt id is `attempt-<32 hex>`, which passes validateEntityId.
- DELIBERATE SCOPE CALL for step 3: resourceStore's write path ends in appendActivity + emit, but both of those would require editing EXISTING unions — ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES (schema.ts:~900-943) and the StateChangeEvent union (StateManager.ts:337, consumed by a WebSocketServer switch) — which the task's "keep it additive / no existing type changes" instruction and the store-layer rails forbid. attemptStore will therefore persist-then-map with no activity row and no emit, and say so in its header; whoever wires attempts into claim/complete/release can add the event types when a consumer exists.
- No ExecutionAttempt or attemptStore exists anywhere in TS/Kotlin source today (only prose in docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-rebuild-*.md and two Serena memories), so nothing to reconcile with a sibling.
- Confirmed for the step-6 FLAG: .gitignore lines 62-67 ignore only .moe/daemon.json, activity.log*, workers/, memory/, messages/, teams/ — neither .moe/resources/ nor a future .moe/attempts/ is listed, so attempts will show in git status (commit attribution's DENY tier still excludes .moe/** except BOARD paths).

implementationPlan.description: DECLARE THE TYPE AND GIVE THE STORE A HOME. In packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts add an exported phase union with exactly the four members running, finalizing, reconciling and closed, and an ExecutionAttempt interface carrying id, taskId, workerId, runnerId, generation, workspace, phase, startedAt and lastPhaseAt as required members, plus optional processStartedAt and host for the later reattachment work. Document generation in a short comment as monotonic per task starting at 1 and never reused, because that is the fencing token the rest of the epic depends on, and document that the optional process fields are advisory - a recorded process start time cannot prove a process is still alive. Keep it additive: no existing type changes, no schemaVersion bump, no migration, exactly as the plan-revision field was added earlier. Then wire the collection into packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts with the two minimal edits that let the store follow the resourceStore idiom rather than growing its own disk access: declare an attempts map beside the resources map at line 367, and load it in StateManager.load beside line 1038 with loadEntities over the attempts directory. loadEntities tolerates a missing directory, so a project that has never opened an attempt loads an empty map. Do NOT add delegating methods on StateManager for attempts in this task, do not touch the state snapshot builder around line 1110, and do not register anything in tools/index.ts or alter claim, complete or release - all explicitly out of scope.

implementationPlan.description: WRITE THE STORE. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts as stateless exported functions taking the StateManager first, mirroring resourceStore, with a header comment explaining what the record is for and why generation exists. Functions: openAttempt, getAttempt, listAttempts, setAttemptPhase, and a currentAttempt helper returning the task's one non-closed attempt or null. openAttempt takes taskId, workerId, runnerId, workspace and an OPTIONAL id, generating one in the repository's existing id shape when absent. Its rules, in this order. First, idempotent repair: if an attempt already exists with the supplied id, and its taskId matches, return the existing record unchanged rather than writing a second file - that is what makes re-running the write path after a crash repair instead of duplicate, and it is why the id is caller-suppliable at all. A supplied id that exists but belongs to a different task is a named conflict error, not a silent adoption. Second, exclusivity: if any attempt for that task is in a phase other than closed, refuse with a named error carrying the existing attempt id, its generation and its phase - never overwrite it. Third, generation: allocate one strictly greater than the maximum generation of EVERY prior attempt for that task including closed ones, so a counter derived from how many attempts currently exist would be wrong after any deletion. Then persist with writeEntity before touching the map, so a failed write leaves no attempt visible anywhere. setAttemptPhase updates phase and lastPhaseAt through the same write-then-map ordering and refuses any change out of closed with a named error, since closed is terminal; deliberately do NOT encode a fuller transition table here - which phase may follow which belongs to the sibling task that wires attempts into claim, complete and release, and guessing it now would be a contract this slice cannot honour. Error handling throughout uses the repository's MoeError with an explicit codeName so a caller can branch on a stable name, reusing an existing numeric code rather than adding an enum member, exactly as the plan-revision work did; validate that taskId, workerId, runnerId and workspace are non-blank strings and that generation never exceeds the safe-integer domain, refusing rather than coercing. Every mutation assumes the caller holds the state mutex, and the header comment must say so, matching resourceStore.
implementationPlan.note:
STORE WRITTEN: packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts, 230 lines, stateless exported functions taking StateManager first, mirroring resourceStore. No StateManager delegating methods, no tool registration, no handler change.

Header comment states, out loud: what the record is for; that generation is a fencing token allocated as max-over-every-prior-attempt + 1 and never from a count, with the reason (a deleted record would reissue a generation an in-flight caller still believes is its own); that THE CALLER HOLDS state.mutex and that the store cannot enforce it alone because the exclusivity check reads the map then writes; the write path writeEntity then map.set, persist before visible; and that recovery is an idempotent re-open rather than a file repair, because writeEntity is atomic temp-and-rename so a torn half-JSON is unreachable — the reachable failure is a record on disk with nothing following it.

API: getAttempt, listAttempts(state, taskId?) in generation order (filters by task when given), currentAttempt(state, taskId) returning the one non-closed attempt or null, openAttempt, setAttemptPhase. Exported MAX_ATTEMPT_GENERATION = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (the MAX_PLAN_REVISION precedent).

openAttempt rules in the required order. (1) Repair: a persisted record under the supplied id IS the attempt — returned unchanged, no second file, no generation advance; a supplied id whose record belongs to another task throws ATTEMPT_ID_TASK_MISMATCH rather than being adopted. (2) Exclusivity: a non-closed attempt for the task throws ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN carrying attemptId, generation and phase; nothing is overwritten. (3) Generation from nextGeneration(), a max over listAttempts(taskId) including closed records, +1; ATTEMPT_GENERATION_EXHAUSTED at the safe-integer ceiling. Then writeEntity, THEN map.set — a failed write leaves the attempt visible nowhere.

setAttemptPhase: unknown phase is INVALID_INPUT first; missing id is ATTEMPT_NOT_FOUND; re-asserting the phase already held is an idempotent no-op with no write (lastPhaseAt records when the phase CHANGED, so a retried close from an exit trap must not churn it); any other change out of closed is ATTEMPT_CLOSED. Deliberately NO fuller transition table — that belongs to the task that wires attempts into claim/complete/release. Updates go through a private copy then the same writeEntity-then-map ordering.

Other decisions worth recording. Error handling is MoeError with an explicit codeName over REUSED numeric codes (STATE_CONFLICT for the three conflicts, NOT_FOUND for the missing attempt, invalidInput for input refusals) — no MoeErrorCode enum member added, matching the PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH/PLAN_REVISION_EXHAUSTED precedent. requireNonBlank refuses blank/non-string taskId, workerId, runnerId, workspace and a blank supplied id before any write. decodeStoredGeneration fails closed on a corrupt persisted generation (non-number, non-safe-integer, < 1) rather than coercing it to 0, because coercing or skipping would let the next allocation reissue a live generation. A caller-supplied id reaches the filesystem only through state.writeEntity, whose validateEntityId rejects path separators before any fs call — the store adds no second validator and no own disk access. No appendActivity and no emit: both need edits to the existing ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES / StateChangeEvent unions and have no consumer yet; the header says so. The advisory processStartedAt/host are copied through only when supplied and are described nowhere as liveness evidence.

Verification so far: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json from packages/moe-daemon, exit 0. Tests are step 4.

implementationPlan.description: TEST IT, INCLUDING THE DURABILITY CASES. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.test.ts using ToolTestHarness, keeping everything in this one file because it is the named verification command for this task. Cover, with exact assertions rather than truthiness: three attempts opened in sequence - each closed before the next opens - receive generations 1, 2 and 3, and a fourth opened after DELETING the middle record still receives 4, which kills the tempting implementation that counts existing records instead of taking the maximum. Opening a second attempt for a task whose current attempt is running, finalizing or reconciling is refused by name, and afterwards the original record on disk is byte-identical and the map holds exactly one attempt for that task. Re-opening with the SAME id returns the same record, writes no second file, and does not advance the generation - the repair case. A supplied id belonging to a different task is refused by name. Durability, in the resourceStore.durability.test.ts style: spy on writeEntity so the first attempts write throws, and assert the accessor returns null AND no file exists under the attempts directory; separately, make a setAttemptPhase write fail and assert both the persisted bytes and the in-memory record still show the old phase. Closed is terminal: every phase change out of closed is refused by name and changes nothing. listAttempts returns generation order and filters by task. A fresh StateManager over the same directory loads the attempts after a restart, which is the whole point of persisting them. Input refusals: blank taskId, blank workerId, blank runnerId and blank workspace each refuse without writing, and an id containing a path separator is rejected by the existing entity-id validation rather than escaping the store directory. Run npx vitest run src/state/attemptStore.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon and require green with nonzero counts.
implementationPlan.note:
TESTS WRITTEN AND GREEN. One file, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.test.ts (the named verification command), 30 tests, ToolTestHarness + two WORKING tasks (task-1, task-2).

Coverage, all with exact assertions (no truthiness):
- generations 1, 2, 3 for three sequential attempts, each closed before the next opens, asserted as the exact tuple [1,2,3] plus the persisted bytes of the third.
- the max-not-count test: after opening three and then DELETING the middle record from BOTH disk and the map (so listAttempts is [1,3]), a fourth gets exactly 4.
- generations are per task: task-2's first attempt is 1 while task-1 already has one.
- an omitted id generates /^attempt-[0-9a-f]{32}$/ and exactly one file.
- exclusivity, parameterised over running, finalizing AND reconciling: the refusal is [ATTEMPT_ALREADY_OPEN], the live record's file is byte-identical (raw string compare, not just deep-equal), listAttempts for that task is exactly [before], and the attempts directory still holds exactly one file. A separate test pins the refusal text carrying id, generation and phase. A third confirms a new attempt IS allowed once the prior one is closed, with generation 2.
- repair: re-opening the same id with a different workerId/workspace returns a record deep-equal to the first, generation still 1, the file's raw bytes unchanged, and still exactly one file.
- a supplied id belonging to a different task is [ATTEMPT_ID_TASK_MISMATCH], task-2 gains no attempt and no second file appears.
- durability, resourceStore.durability.test.ts style (failNextAttemptWrite spies writeEntity to throw once for kind 'attempts', then delegate): a failed initial write leaves getAttempt null, currentAttempt null AND no file on disk; a failed setAttemptPhase write leaves both the persisted bytes and the in-memory record deep-equal to before with phase still 'running'.
- setAttemptPhase: a real change stamps a later lastPhaseAt, keeps startedAt, and persists the exact record; closed is terminal for all three non-closed targets ([ATTEMPT_CLOSED], disk and memory unchanged); re-closing a closed attempt is a no-op that calls writeEntity zero times; an unknown id is [ATTEMPT_NOT_FOUND]; an unknown phase value is [INVALID_INPUT] and leaves the record running.
- listAttempts in generation order, filtered by task, unfiltered over both tasks, empty for an unknown task; currentAttempt null when everything is closed.
- restart: a fresh StateManager over the same directory loads both records (size 2, each deep-equal to what was persisted, currentAttempt identifies the live one), and opening again after closing the live one yields generation 3 — the generation is not reissued across a restart.
- a project that never opened an attempt has an empty map and NO attempts directory (proves loadEntities tolerates the missing dir and that nothing scaffolds it).
- input refusals, parameterised: blank taskId/workerId/runnerId/workspace each throw [INVALID_INPUT] Invalid <field> with the map empty and zero files; an id of '../../escaped' is refused by the existing entity-id validation ([INVALID_INPUT] Invalid entityId) with no file written at the project root or in .moe.
- advisory hints: absent when not supplied (key absence, not undefined), copied through and persisted when supplied.

Test-env note worth keeping: the lastPhaseAt test uses vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] }) inside a try/finally. Faking setTimeout too would stall atomicWriteJsonAsync's rename-retry backoff with nothing left to advance it, which is a real hang risk on Windows where that retry actually fires.

Verification (exit code captured in a separate statement, per the filtered-pipeline trap): `npx vitest run src/state/attemptStore.test.ts` from packages/moe-daemon -> exit 0, "Test Files 1 passed (1)", "Tests 30 passed (30)", 868ms.

implementationPlan.description: RED PROOF BY MUTATION, THEN THE FULL SUITE. This is a new store, so there is no old behavior to fail against directly - establish the red by mutation instead, restoring the checkout after each and re-verifying with a separate git status call rather than trusting the edit. Perform at least these four and name the test that fails for each: remove the non-closed exclusivity guard so a second attempt silently overwrites a running one; derive the generation from the count of existing attempts instead of the maximum, which must break the delete-then-open case; set the map before calling writeEntity, which must break both injected-failure cases; and make the idempotent re-open write a fresh record, which must break the repair case and the generation assertion together. Then run the full daemon suite from the repository root - Windows npm.cmd - and require exit 0 with counts at least as high as before this change, since a store added at the state layer must not disturb anything else. The vitest output on this box is buried in logger noise, so filter for the summary lines but capture the exit code in a separate statement, because a filtered pipeline swallows it. implementationPlan.description: ADVERSARIAL REVIEW AND HANDOFF. Read the diff as an attacker. Does every mutation persist before it becomes visible, so a crash can never expose an attempt that is not on disk? Can two opens for the same task ever both succeed - including the ordering where one is mid-write - given that callers hold the state mutex, and does the header comment say that requirement out loud? Is a generation ever reused after a deletion, a restart or a closed attempt? Can a caller-supplied id reach the filesystem without passing the existing entity-id validation? Is closed genuinely terminal? Does the code avoid claiming anything it cannot know - specifically, a recorded process start time and host are advisory hints for later reattachment and must not be described anywhere as proof that a process is alive, which the epic notes call out explicitly. Confirm the rails held: nothing was registered in tools/index.ts, no claim, complete or release handler changed, no database or migration was introduced, no schemaVersion bump, and the store uses writeEntity and loadEntities rather than its own disk access. One thing to FLAG rather than fix: the new attempts directory is runtime state like workers and messages, but it is not in the repository ignore list, so it will show up in git status; the commit attribution already excludes everything under the state directory except board paths, so nothing will be committed by accident - note it in the completion summary as a follow-up for whoever owns the ignore list rather than editing it here. Complete through moe.complete_task with the recorded verification evidence and the mutation proofs, listing every modified path in modifiedFiles, and state plainly that this task adds the record and its store only - claim, complete and release wiring belong to the sibling tasks that depend on it.
implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW DONE. One real change came out of it; the rest are recorded boundaries.

CHANGED: openAttempt was 55 lines, over the 50-line bar. Extracted two named helpers — repairExisting() (returns the persisted record or null, throws ATTEMPT_ID_TASK_MISMATCH) and assertNoOpenAttempt() — leaving openAttempt at 34 lines and setAttemptPhase at 35. Behaviour identical: 30/30 still pass, tsc exit 0, full suite re-run exit 0 with Test Files 105 passed, Tests 1281 passed. The extraction also gave the two subtle contracts a docstring each, including the check-then-act note on exclusivity pointing at the mutex requirement.

Checklist answers.
- Persist-before-visible: both write paths are writeEntity then map.set, with no await between the checks and the write, so a throw leaves nothing published. Proved by mutation M3 (reversing the order broke both injected-failure tests).
- Two concurrent opens: exclusivity is a check-then-act over the in-memory map, so it holds ONLY because the caller holds state.mutex. The header says that out loud and now so does assertNoOpenAttempt. Within one call the first await is writeEntity, after both checks, so under the reentrant mutex two dispatches cannot interleave. The store cannot enforce this alone and does not pretend to.
- Generation reuse: never. nextGeneration takes the max over listAttempts(taskId) including closed records, and the record is persisted, so a deletion, a close and a restart are all covered (the delete-then-open test and the restart test assert 4 and 3 respectively). decodeStoredGeneration fails closed on a corrupt stored value rather than coercing it to 0, which would otherwise reissue a live generation.
- Caller-supplied id reaching the filesystem: only through state.writeEntity, whose validateEntityId rejects anything outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] and anything over 128 chars before any fs call. Nothing is trimmed or normalised first, so '../../escaped' and 'attempt-a ' both fail closed rather than being silently repaired into a different id. Tested.
- Closed terminal: yes. Any non-closed target from closed is ATTEMPT_CLOSED with nothing written; closed->closed is an explicit no-op that calls writeEntity zero times (asserted with a spy), because lastPhaseAt means 'when the phase changed' and a retried close from an exit trap must not churn it.
- Liveness language: audited by grep. The only three mentions of alive/liveness/proof in my diff all say the opposite — processStartedAt and host are advisory reattachment hints that CANNOT prove a process is alive and that nothing may treat as proof.

BOUNDARIES RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED (all intentional, all relevant to the sibling that wires this in):
1. A repair returns the persisted record and deliberately ignores the caller's other params — a re-open carrying a different workspace or workerId does not rewrite history. Now stated in repairExisting's docstring; a caller that cares must compare the fields itself.
2. openAttempt does not require the task to exist. Whether an attempt may outlive its task is claim/complete/release policy, not store policy; now stated in the docstring.
3. Reads (getAttempt/listAttempts/currentAttempt and the repair return) hand back the live map object, exactly as resourceStore's getResource does. In-place mutation by a caller would desync memory from disk. Every write path here builds a fresh object or a shallow copy of an all-primitive record, so the store itself never aliases.
4. The repair key is the in-memory map, so it assumes the map reflects disk. True after load() and while the daemon is sole writer; an externally written .moe/attempts file that predates no reload would be overwritten. Identical assumption to resourceStore's getOrCreateResource, and hand-editing .moe/ is already forbidden.
5. workspace, workerId and runnerId are bounded only by non-blankness. String-length sanitation in this repo lives at the tool layer, which is out of scope here.

RAILS CONFIRMED by git status and grep: tools/index.ts, claimNextTask.ts, completeTask.ts and releaseTask.ts are all untouched (empty porcelain output for those paths); CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION is still 6; no database, no migration; the store imports no fs/path and calls no atomicWrite — writeEntity and loadEntities only; no ACTIVITY_EVENT_TYPES or StateChangeEvent edit. My whole diff is schema.ts +50, StateManager.ts +6 and the two new files. Everything else in git status (the JetBrains Kotlin files, tools/enterGovernance.*, the board JSON) belongs to other live sessions and was not touched, reverted or staged.

Scope clarification for the worker and QA: the plan-size warning says 6 distinct files, but only FOUR are edited. Step 1 is read-only exploration and lists state/resourceStore.ts and state/persistence.ts purely as required reading; they must not be modified.

Files actually edited: types/schema.ts (additive ExecutionAttempt type and phase union), state/StateManager.ts (two lines only, an attempts map beside resources and one loadEntities call in load), new state/attemptStore.ts, new state/attemptStore.test.ts.

Two design points worth stating up front because they decide the implementation. First, the attempt id is caller-suppliable on purpose: that is what makes re-opening after a crash idempotent, which is how the repair-not-duplicate criterion is met without a file-repair routine. writeEntity already writes atomically through a temp file and rename, so a torn JSON file is not the failure mode to design for; a record that reached disk with nothing following it is. Second, the generation must be the maximum prior generation plus one, never a count of existing records, or a deletion reissues a used fencing token. Both have dedicated tests and both are on the mutation red list.

Deliberately not decided here: the full phase transition table. This slice enforces only that closed is terminal. Which phase may follow which belongs to the sibling that wires attempts into claim, complete and release.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Generating the attempt id inside the store with no caller override - rejected: then a crashed open can only be recovered by scanning for a matching record, and the DONE criterion asking for repair rather than duplication has no clean implementation. A caller-suppliable id makes re-open idempotent by construction. Deriving the generation from the number of existing attempts - rejected and explicitly tested against: after any deletion it would reissue a used generation, which is fatal for a fencing token. Encoding a full phase transition table now - rejected: which phase may follow which is decided by the sibling that wires attempts into claim, complete and release, so this slice enforces only that closed is terminal and leaves the rest to the task that actually knows. Giving StateManager delegating methods for attempts - rejected as premature: no caller exists yet, and the task rails keep this to the store layer. Adding a schemaVersion bump or migration - rejected by an epic rail and unnecessary for a purely additive record.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured live on 2026-09-11. writeEntity already handles three things this task would otherwise have to build: it validates the entity id against path traversal, it creates the kind directory with a recursive mkdir, and it finishes with an atomic temp-file-and-rename write. That last point reshapes the durability design - a torn half-written JSON file is not the failure mode to defend against; the real one is a record that reached disk before the process died with nothing following it, which is why the repair path is an idempotent re-open keyed on a caller-suppliable id rather than a file-repair routine. loadEntities tolerates a missing directory, so a project that has never opened an attempt simply loads an empty map and the new directory needs no scaffolding. The resourceStore header states the contract this store must copy verbatim: stateless functions taking the state handle first, every mutation under the state mutex, and writeEntity then map.set then activity then emit. Two small StateManager edits are unavoidable and in scope - a map field and one load line - because without them the store would need its own disk access, which the second task rail forbids as a second persistence idiom. MoeError accepts an explicit codeName, so the named refusals here need no enum member, exactly as the plan-revision work established.
planningNotes.risks: The likeliest wrong implementation is a generation derived from a count rather than a maximum; the delete-then-open test exists specifically to kill it. The second is setting the map before the write, which would expose an attempt that is not durable - both injected-failure tests exist to kill that. Exclusivity depends on callers holding the state mutex; the store cannot enforce it alone, so the header comment must say so, matching resourceStore. Do not let the optional process start time and host be described as proof of liveness anywhere - the epic notes are explicit that a JSON record cannot stop or detect a running external process, and this task must not seed language that a later slice would inherit as a false guarantee. Keep generation inside the safe-integer domain, shared with the Kotlin client's Long. Stay at the store layer: no tool registration, no handler changes, no snapshot-builder change. Finally, the new attempts directory is runtime state that is not in the ignore list, so it will appear in git status - flag it in the completion summary rather than editing the ignore list, since commit attribution already excludes that tree except for board paths.
